scriptEchoArtifact_ANDITSGENERALFORM.theArtifact: A GitHub Actions job log echoes the SOURCE of every run: block into the log, inside the ##[group]Run ... ##[endgroup] region, before that step produces any output. Grepping the job log therefore matches the script's own text as well as the script's output, and any count taken over the whole log is inflated by an amount that depends on how often the pattern appears in the source.
scriptEchoArtifact_ANDITSGENERALFORM.measuredOnThisLog: The job log is 3121 lines. The paid step's script source occupies lines 229 to 447; its output runs 448 to 3065. Whole-log versus output-only counts: 'cost:' 16 versus 6, so a naive count inflates by 167 percent; '===== running test:' 7 versus 6; 'MEASURED' 41 versus 13.
scriptEchoArtifact_ANDITSGENERALFORM.theSharperCase_falsePOSITIVES_forEventsT: Five strings that a reader would take as evidence of an abort appear ONLY in echoed source and NEVER in output: 'BUDGET EXHAUSTED' 1 whole / 0 output, 'HALT' 2 / 0, 'SKIPPED:' 1 / 0, 'accounting' 7 / 0, '::warning::' 2 / 0. '::error::' appears 14 times whole and 0 times in output, and 8 of those 14 are not even in the paid step: they are the echoed sources of the three guard steps at lines 119 to 179. A whole-log grep for any of these reports a hit on a run where the event did not occur.
scriptEchoArtifact_ANDITSGENERALFORM.consequenceForThisArtifact: Every count in this RESOLUTION was taken from lines 448 to 3065 only. Anyone re-deriving these figures must apply the same restriction or they will not reproduce them.
scriptEchoArtifact_ANDITSGENERALFORM.generalForm: An instrument that reads a transcript containing its own subject's source code cannot distinguish description from occurrence. This is the same shape as the repo's standing rule that lines are not occurrences and that a check must measure its property rather than a correlate.

costBand_andItsDerivation: Two point predictions and one upper bound. (A) EMPIRICAL, the sum of each detector's most recent measured per-detector run: 0.2713 + 0.9204 + 1.2001 + 1.2032 + 1.5967 + 0.6457 = $5.8374. (B) FLAT CONSTANT across all 710 calls at $0.00828: $5.8788. (C) UPPER BOUND from measure:stage3-calls at N=5: $6.41, self-labelled CONSERVATIVE UPPER and leaning high, and it prices 720 calls because it includes idor-multi's 10, which `all` does not run. BAND: $5.84 to $6.41.
ceiling: $8.00, set ABOVE BOTH point predictions AND the upper bound together, never above ours alone. It clears (C) $6.41 by 25 percent and clears (A) inflated by the flat constant's known upper error of +17.0 percent, which is $6.8298, by 17 percent. It sits below the workflow guard's own $10.00 sanity bound, so it is a deliberately stated figure rather than the maximum. IT IS DELIBERATELY NOT TIGHTER: since #166 the ceiling bounds the RUN rather than each detector, so an abort now TRUNCATES the run and leaves detectors unrun with coverage unknown. A ceiling set at the band would abort merely at the high end of known error and forfeit the very simultaneity this run is being bought to establish.
canThisRunDISCRIMINATE_betweenCostModels: NO, AND THIS IS PRE-COMMITTED BEFORE THE NUMBER EXISTS. The two point candidates, the empirical sum ($5.8374) and the flat constant ($5.8788), sit 0.71 percent apart. The only cross-window noise evidence is n=1 (positive/11 on an identical request drifted +16.4 percent in output length over five weeks, which at a 40-55 percent output share moves a total by 6.6-9.0 percent). A 0.71 percent gap against a 6.6-9.0 percent noise floor cannot be resolved by one sample. NO CORROBORATION OF ANY COST MODEL MAY BE CLAIMED FROM THIS RUN'S COST, HOWEVER IT LANDS, including if it lands on one of them exactly. The most this run can do is falsify (C) as an upper bound, by exceeding $6.41. Anyone later citing this run as evidence for a cost model is citing a claim its own pre-registration refused in advance.

FIRST_LIVE_EXERCISE_OF_THE_RUN_BUDGET_ME: THIS RUN IS THE FIRST TO USE #166's PER-RUN BUDGET, AND THAT MECHANISM HAS NEVER RUN AGAINST A REAL DETECTOR. It was merged the same day as this pre-registration (squash 5d1c8cae) and verified only against a stub npm supplying canned cost lines. The controls' own stated limit is that they prove the REFUSAL TO START when the remainder is exhausted, and cannot prove an in-process abort at a handed ceiling. Every dispatch before this one was single-detector, where the remainder on the only iteration equals the budget and the handoff is a no-op, so nothing in the run history exercises it either.
howAMISFIRE_wouldLOOK: The budget is carried between six separate processes by the shell variable measured_total, which is parsed out of each detector's `cost:` line. If that parse under-counts, the next detector is handed a remainder LARGER than it should be and the run bound is breached quietly. If it over-counts, or if a cost line is mis-read as a smaller figure than it is, a detector is handed a ceiling FAR BELOW its real cost, its SpendGuard throws SpendCeilingExceeded early, and the run truncates with detectors unrun. THE SECOND IS THE EXPENSIVE ONE: the money for the detectors that already ran is spent, the authorization is consumed, and the simultaneity this run exists to establish is forfeited.
howALATER_READER_TELLS_A_GENUINE_BUDGET_: The workflow ECHOES THE HANDED CEILING ON EVERY INVOCATION ('running test:<d> (ceiling for this invocation: $X)'), and the step summary records each detector's cost mode and measured amount. The sequence is therefore inspectable after the fact. THE IDENTITY TO CHECK IS: ceiling_k == run budget minus the sum of measured amounts for detectors 1..k-1, at every k. If that identity holds at every step and the last handed ceiling was genuinely exhausted, the budget stop is REAL and the band was simply too low. If the identity breaks anywhere, the arithmetic misfired and the stop is an APPARATUS DEFECT, not a cost finding. Do not read a truncated run as evidence about spend until that identity has been checked line by line.
aTRUNCATION_CONSUMES_THE_AUTHORIZATION_W: Stated plainly because it is the whole risk of going first: a budget stop or an accounting stop leaves the owner having paid for the detectors that ran while holding no simultaneity result, because simultaneity is a property of ALL SIX at one SHA and is not divisible. Partial coverage does not part-establish it. The unrun detectors must be reported NOT STARTED with coverage UNKNOWN, never as passing and never as $0 tested.
theACCOUNTING_STOP_IS_ALSO_A_TRUNCATION_: #166 halts the run if any detector reports a cost mode other than MEASURED or NOCALLS, because MIXED is a stated lower bound and NO LINE / NOT MEASURED / UNRECOGNIZED contribute zero against unknown real spend, so the next remainder could not be computed soundly. A LEGITIMATELY PARTIALLY-PRICED DETECTOR THEREFORE TRUNCATES THIS RUN. Historical rate of that event: ZERO, across 590 priced calls in the four artifact-backed runs (admin-check 150/150, webhook-unverified 170/170, auth-bypass 185/185, env-exposure 85/85, every call priced). It is pre-registered rather than engineered away: the alternative, continuing on MIXED by estimating the unpriced calls, would put a made-up number inside a spend guard, which is the failure mode costPerLlmCallUsd already refuses a default for.
whatWASdoneFREE_toREDUCE_thisRisk: One thing, and it is real. The workflow's classify() parser was run verbatim against the ACTUAL cost lines the REAL harness emits for all six detectors, captured free from the measure:stage3-calls run at 5d1c8cae. All six parse as MEASURED with the dollar amount correctly extracted, despite the line carrying a trailing parenthetical NOTE. This closes the 'a mode the classifier does not recognise' branch for the shape the harness actually produces on all six, using real output rather than stub output.
whatNOTHING_FREE_CAN_REDUCE: The amounts in that free check are $0.0000, because the spy returns synthetic zero-token responses, so measured_total never advances and THE REMAINDER SEQUENCE IS NOT EXERCISED against real output. Nothing free can produce a nonzero MEASURED line: it requires real token usage, and the replay corpus carries no usage fields at all, so a replay run emits NOT MEASURED and would trip the accounting stop rather than rehearse the handoff. The in-process abort likewise cannot be exercised without spending. THERE IS NO FURTHER FREE MITIGATION; the remaining risk is accepted knowingly and is the price of being first.

threeExits_whatEachCONSUMES_andEARNS.1_verdictFailure_CONTINUES: One or more detectors fail their gate. Since #166 the loop RECORDS the failure and CONTINUES, and the run exits non-zero after all six have reported. CONSUMES: the full run, about $5.84 to $6.41, bounded by the $8.00 budget. EARNS: the complete simultaneity picture at one SHA including which detectors failed and which held. This is the outcome the loop fix was bought for.
threeExits_whatEachCONSUMES_andEARNS.2_budgetStop_HALTS: Measured spend reaches the $8.00 budget, so the next detector is not started. CONSUMES: up to $8.00 plus at most one call of overshoot, since SpendGuard throws when spend EXCEEDS the ceiling, after the crossing call is priced. EARNS: partial coverage, plus the knowledge that the budget was set too low. The unrun detectors are reported NOT STARTED with coverage UNKNOWN, never as passing and never as $0 tested.
threeExits_whatEachCONSUMES_andEARNS.3_accountingStop_HALTS: A detector reports a cost mode other than MEASURED or NOCALLS, so the remaining budget cannot be computed soundly and the run halts before its successors. CONSUMES: the spend of the detectors that ran, PLUS an unknown amount for the detector that failed to report. EARNS: partial coverage, and a loud signal that the harness's cost-line shape has changed and the workflow's classify() parser needs updating. An unreadable cost line is treated as unknown spend, never as zero.
threeExits_whatEachCONSUMES_andEARNS.4_skipped_HALTS_at_zero: Any detector prints a SKIPPED marker, meaning the key guard was bypassed and it tested nothing. Halts at once. CONSUMES: nothing. EARNS: nothing except the knowledge that the key was absent. Deliberately NOT counted as a failed detector, because a detector that tested nothing did not fail.

statedResidualsOnTheAPPARATUS: The EXIT trap that writes the spend footer runs on exits and signals but NOT on SIGKILL, so a hard 120-minute timeout kill still loses the footer and the money would be spent with the total unwritten. The run is bounded by call count rather than by the clock, so a raised timeout does not raise maximum spend.

Delete the secret the moment the paid step goes terminal, then verify 404 by name plus zero across repo Actions, variables, Dependabot, repo Codespaces and all environments, recording any probe that fails for want of scope as a FAILURE and never as a zero.
